A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in
`prunedTrees`, so 4200 installed package manifests are one record, never 4200
units. **The anchor is recorded because the tree was observed, not because a
marker was found inside it** (XA-02 / CR-25): a pruned tree holding no manifest
is still one row, taken from the admitted directory observation discovery
already holds. Discovery still never descends into a pruned tree - not to count
markers and not to find a nested anchor; the outermost pruned segment is the
only anchor. The earlier promise to record *the number of markers it hid* is
withdrawn: a count over an unenumerated tree is not an observation. The row is
the closed `{path, reason, markerCount, markerCountBasis}` (version 2).
`markerCountBasis` is `observed-inventory` only when the supplier declares that
its marker inventory enumerated inside pruned trees, and then `markerCount` is
exact **over that supplied inventory alone**; otherwise the basis is
`not-enumerated` and `markerCount` is `null`. An anchor whose own directory
observation could not be established is reported with a null count on the same
rule. Zero observed is never zero hidden. Count and basis are provenance: they
select no unit, bound no work, enter no Coverage and enter no scope descriptor,
though they do change the exact bytes of the provenance and boundary records and
therefore any operational digest taken over them. Version-1 records keep their
bytes and are read as version 1.

Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful
empty scope; later syntax scanners cannot read their uncustodied source.

Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful
empty scope; later syntax scanners cannot read their uncustodied source. A
custody- or depth-excluded directory is therefore never examined-clean Coverage.
The downward unit-depth bound reuses the same 256-level constant as the upward
ancestor walk: a unit directory deeper than 256 segments below the selected root
is excluded with reason `DEPTH` and exported to the language-unit instrument in
`custodyExcludedUnits`, so both instruments select the same directories. It is
an exclusion with unknown standing, not a work budget. **Bounding the host
observation itself - how many directory and marker entries discovery may admit -
is the observation-admission and qualification responsibility, not this cap.**
The 4096 unit cap was never an input bound: the shared rule materialises and
sorts the supplied inventory before comparing cardinality, both before and after
the XA-01 correction. No public work-budget flag is introduced here, and the
synthetic trusted fs-map instrument accepting a large array is not a product
limit. Counting custody- and depth-excluded directories toward the cap, rather
than counting admitted units, is a **separately reviewable policy option that is
NOT selected here**; it would turn present ACCEPT results into refusals and is
not required to fix XA-01.
